title: Ship the quest-board mod in the opum-quest plugin (OPAG-1074)
description: Operator instruction, 2026-10-02 (relayed by opum-doc as ODOC-OP-2026-10-02-10; tracked in opum-agent as OPAG-1074): build the Quest board mod and ship it in the opum-quest plugin. Design brief: opum-doc docs/reference/quest-board-mod-design-brief.md, merged by opum-ai/opum-doc#619 and read at opum-doc dev 4fbc7578. Prototype: opum-docs session-local dev-mods folder, copied in here as the starting point. The mod is a hooks module plus its contract and tests, shipped inside the opum-quest plugin cut from this repository, with the marketplace pin moving to the release that carries it. Two questions stay with the operator and are not decided here: edits from a fleet view, and the actor identity for pane edits. This task covers the build and its landing only; the release is its own task.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The opum-quest plugin ships the quest-board hooks module: hooks/hooks.json names one module, and .claude-plugin/plugin.json declares the modules state contract and the pane actor option.

claude plugin validate on the repository root reports the plugin valid on the builds pinned Claude Code version, and the module typechecks against the engine declaration with no errors; both exact commands and their results are recorded on the task.
The mod test suite passes under claude plugin test across the terminal and desktop surfaces, and a repo gate runs it so a failing mod test fails the gate rather than passing unrun.
The fleet view reads a discovered repository set rather than a hardcoded list, configurable through the plugins userConfig, with the sessions own repository always included.

The board offers the repository-true read (quest task list --across-refs) as a toggle, marks a task whose states disagree across refs, and shows an incomplete coverage read as incomplete rather than as an empty result.

A pane write happens only in the sessions own repository, through Quest lifecycle commands, with an explicit actor on every write and --if-revision on field edits; a test asserts the argv of each write.
The repositorys own checks exit 0 with the mod files present, and the repo test suite neither collects nor breaks on the mod test files.
The repositorys lore docs describe the mod and record its design decisions, and lore check exits 0.
The change lands on dev by a squash-merged pull request that cites the run validating its deliverable, and this task is closed in that PR.

plan: Branch feat/QCLI-431-quest-board-mod off origin/dev, carrying this task record on the first commit (orchestrator, 2026-10-02).

Copy the opum-doc prototype into the plugin root: hooks/hooks.json, hooks/register.tsx, types/index.d.ts, mod tests; rename the state namespace and mount name to the plugin opum-quest; merge userConfig and the types contract into .claude-plugin/plugin.json.

Apply the brief recommendations: repository-true reads via quest task list --across-refs as a toggle with cross-ref state merge and coverage surfaced; repository discovery through userConfig with the sessions own repo always included; keep the write boundary, the Quest lifecycle commands and the mobile line.

Add scripts/mod-test.mjs: stage the plugins shipped files into a temp dir and run claude plugin validate, claude plugin test and tsc against the engine types there; wire it into bun run check and into prepublish source gates, installing the pinned CLI in the CI job.
Keep the repos own suite off the mod tests (bun --path-ignore-patterns) and gitignore the engine-written .claude-plugin/types.

Write the lore Reference doc for the mod, recording the execution choices and the alternatives rejected (layout with the staged-files runner over a git-subdir move; the refs toggle default; discovery) and the deferred keyboard card movement. No ADR: component design records are the operators, and the orchestrator ruled on 2026-10-02 that these are execution choices recorded here and on this task. lore check exits 0.
Record validate/test/tsc/check evidence on this task, open the PR into dev, and close this task in it.
implementationNotes: SCOPE AND RECORDING SHAPE, settled 2026-10-02 with the orchestrator before building. (1) Keyboard card movement on the kanban (brief recommendation 5) is DEFERRED, and that is the orchestrators scope call: the list tab already carries every edit, and card movement is new behaviour and new test surface the operator did not ask for; opum-doc is being told so the operator can bring it back. (2) The fleet-edit question from the brief is NOT REACHED: v1 keeps the fleet view read-only, so there is nothing to decide; recorded as deliberately out of scope rather than unfinished. (3) The actor identity for pane edits is the operators and is still open; it goes to the orchestrator as an A/B when the manifests default is final. (4) No ADR for the layout or the test-runner choice: under the operating models design authority every ADR is the operators, including one about a single component, so these are recorded as execution choices in the repos own Reference doc and here, with the alternatives that were rejected and why.

HANDOFF, 2026-10-02, mid-build. The mod is written, tested and pushed; the remaining work is wiring, docs and the close. Branch feat/QCLI-431-quest-board-mod, head 65c2fcaf, pushed; draft PR opum-ai/quest-cli#481 (draft because the build is unfinished, not because anything needs review yet). No teammate is live. Nothing is blocked on a person except the actor-identity question, which is not yet asked.

WHAT IS DONE AND VERIFIED (all on this branch, Claude Code 2.1.287, run by node scripts/mod-test.mjs, which stages the files the plugin ships into a temp directory and runs the three tools against the stage):
- claude plugin validate: passed. It reports the hooks, the calls and the four state keys, and holds them to types/index.d.ts.
- claude plugin test: 13 pass, 0 fail, across four files (board, edit, discovery and the parsers). The drawing tests loop over terminal and desktop.
- tsc against the engine declaration: clean (exit 0). The declaration used is the one matching the running CLI -- /tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.287/<hash>/plugin-authoring/types/claude-code.d.ts, whose first line names 2.1.287. The runner prefers an exact version match and falls back to the newest, naming which it used.
- bun test --path-ignore-patterns=tests/**: verified that bare bun test DOES collect tests/board.test.tsx (1 error, 1 fail) and that the flag excludes it (29 pass on test/domain with the flag on).

WHAT THE MOD IS: hooks/register.tsx (the pane), hooks/quest.ts (argv building, both task-list parsers, discovery -- split out so it is testable without a surface), types/index.d.ts (the state contract and the drawn shapes), tests/ (four files), .claude-plugin/plugin.json (gained the types contract, the actor option and root/repos options), scripts/mod-test.mjs.

DECISIONS ALREADY MADE, with reasons, for the successor and for the record:
1. Layout: the plugin root stays the repository root, so opum-marketplace keeps moving only the ref pin. The alternative, a git-subdir source with the plugin in a subdirectory, gives claude plugin test a clean folder but restructures a shipped plugin and changes another repository's entry shape; it was rejected for that reason, not because it does not work. The cost accepted: the engine scans every *.test.ts under the directory it is given, so the mod tests run against a stage built by scripts/mod-test.mjs rather than against the checkout. Recorded as an execution choice, NOT an ADR: the orchestrator ruled on 2026-10-02 that component design records are the operator's.
2. Brief recommendation 5 (keyboard card movement on the kanban) is DEFERRED by the orchestrator's scope call; the list tab carries every edit.
3. The fleet-edit question is NOT REACHED: v1 keeps the fleet view read-only.
4. The actor identity for pane edits is still the operator's and is NOT decided. The manifest currently ships the prototype's default (jdnewhouse, --actor-kind human, configurable). The orchestrator expects an A/B with the recommendation first and the quality, speed and cost of each side, sent to opum-agent, not asked in this pane.

WHAT IS LEFT, in the order the plan recorded on this task lists it:
a. Wire scripts/mod-test.mjs into bun run check (a test:mod script exists; check does not call it yet) and into the source gates in scripts/qualification/prepublish.mjs (a new gate calling bun run test:mod), and install the pinned CLI in .github/workflows/prepublication-qualification.yml next to the existing npm install --global @salient-ai/jira-cli line. Add hooks/**, types/**, tests/**, scripts/mod-test.mjs and .claude-plugin/** to that workflow's push paths. This is the one step whose CI behaviour is unverified from here: claude plugin test has only been run on this machine. Prove it rejects as well as accepts -- break one test deliberately and confirm the gate goes red with the mod error and nothing else.
b. Bring hooks/**, types/** and tests/** into biome.json files.includes, the lint and format:check script paths in package.json, and the directory list in scripts/test-repository-check-scope.mjs, then run lint and format:check.
c. Write the lore Reference doc for the mod in this repository's docs bundle (lore new, then lore link to QCLI-431; lore check must exit 0). It carries the choices in 1 to 4 above and the alternatives rejected.
d. Record the evidence above on this task, ask the actor-identity A/B through opum-agent, then open the PR for review (it is a draft now), let the required checks report on the head, squash-merge, delete the local branch, and close this task in that PR with the run that validated the deliverable named.

GOTCHAS THAT COST TIME HERE, so they do not cost it again:
- session.start does NOT fire under claude plugin test. Discovery ran only there at first, so a kit-mounted pane drew an empty fleet -- and an empty fleet looks exactly like a fleet with nothing in it. Discovery is now lazy (ensureFleet, called from session.start and from the first read). The prototype never hit this because its repo list was a constant.
- A noun of $ cannot be passed as a value: the validator refuses reposUnder($.fs, root). The two fs calls are spelled out at the call site in an adapter.
- atom() requires literal plugin and key at the call site; a const does not satisfy the scan.
- A refresh asked for while one is in flight was silently dropped (the prototype returned early); it is now queued and the read repeats, without which a toggle pressed mid-read leaves the old scope drawn.
- The engine writes its declaration beside a mod only when a session loads that mod from a folder the person owns; claude plugin test does NOT write one, so the typecheck needs the bundled skill copy or a laid .claude-plugin/types/ (now gitignored).

See the last paragraph.
